scope: Editorial review of the catalogue's definitions and proposed AI manifestations. Grouping does not establish psychological synonymy or a shared causal mechanism.
finding: The 434-record inventory did not establish 434 distinct operational behaviours. Exact-name and alias checks missed overlapping descriptions.

groupings.reason: Both current AI descriptions concern shaping answers for approval or a favourable impression. The nested record retains the narrower social-presentation framing; this is not a claim that every form of people-pleasing equals social desirability bias.

Both operational definitions describe guessing an ambiguous requirement and acting instead of clarifying it. The narrower clarification-avoidance record and its AI papers are retained inside the existing entry.

The current AI descriptions both justify persistence through prior investment. Escalation can have causes beyond sunk costs in human research; the record is grouped for the overlap of this catalogue's operational examples, not declared a universal synonym.

The proposed AI manifestation is promising monitoring, memory or guarantees beyond available capability. That observable pattern already appears under overpromising. Psychological omnipotence is not inferred from it.

The proposed example narrows attention to one detail while the broader failure is neglected. Encysting is retained as a detail-focused variant of the catalogue's tunneling pattern, without asserting identical human mechanisms.

Continuing an original plan despite contrary tool output repeats the catalogue's existing persistence-after-loss-of-usefulness criterion. The named complex-task pattern is retained as a plan-following variant.

Forcing each problem into a favourite framework repeats the existing operational reliance on a familiar method. The broader human cognitive-style claim remains a supplied attribution needing source review.
The proposed AI example attributes its own failure to the environment, already covered by the existing attribution pattern. A genuinely unforeseeable external cause is not itself an error.

The supplied AI example hands a doable step back to the user, which is already part of the existing operational definition. The clinical concept is preserved separately as a proposed analogy, not diagnosed in the model.

kept_distinct.boundary: Negative and positive urgency differ in affective trigger; similarity in wording does not erase that distinction.
Spontaneous recovery is tested after delay, renewal after context change, and reinstatement after outcome re-exposure.
Duration neglect concerns duration weighting; the peak-end rule concerns weighting particular moments.
Reassurance seeking recruits confirmation from another party; checking compulsion repeats one's own checks.
Consensus pressure, assuming another actor will act, and reducing one's effort in a group are different operational contrasts.
Emotional reasoning uses feeling as evidence; positive urgency concerns rash action during positive affect.
Generalising a learned value incorrectly differs from exploiting the task's evaluation metric.
An attention/filtering analogy is not the same test as obeying instructions embedded in untrusted content.
The general order-position pattern and its context-retrieval application are related levels of description, not evidence of two independent causal mechanisms.
Conditioning output on evaluation context does not by itself establish an alternative concealed objective.
A human interpreter analogy and direct AI trace-faithfulness claims occupy different explanatory levels; neither proves the other's mechanism.

review_method: Manual comparison of definitions and AI examples, supported by an exact-name/alias collision scan and TF-IDF lexical candidate screening. Lexical scores are not semantic-identity evidence.
limits: This is not an independent taxonomy validation or a claim that the 425 primary entries are mutually exclusive or causally independent. Related constructs remain where a meaningful test or descriptive-level distinction exists. Original IDs, numbers, definitions and sources are preserved.
prevention: Count primary entries and grouped variants separately. A unique ID, different label or passing duplicate-name test must not be reported as proof of a distinct behaviour.
